newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Sime Bank and some others.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Sime Bank and some others.

text.p: Sime International Bank (L), a unit of Sime Bank, launched a US$100 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue into Asian debt markets on Monday.
The three-year certificates pay a margin of 23.5 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 27 basis points to top tier managers.
Fuji International Finance (HK), Development Bank of Singapore and LTCB Asia are arrangers.

Bankers said they expect Japanese and European investors to be attracted to the issue. Other potential investors, notably Korean banks, have higher funding costs and might find the issue too tightly priced, they said.
The deal, which is the borrower's debut issue, is attractive because of the strength of its ultimate parent, conglomerate Sime Darby, a syndicate manager at one of the arranging banks said.
In other news, the People's Republic of China has mandated HongKong Bank China Services and DKB Hong Kong to arrange a US$100 million loan.
The amortising loan has a final maturity of 15 years. Proceeds will be used for a new power plant in China's central Henan province.

Representatives from Croatia were in Hong Kong today on the first stop of a worldwide roadshow to promote the country's debut Eurobond. The US$250 million bond will have a five-year maturity but pricing details are not yet available.
Merrill Lynch and Union Bank of Switzerland are joint lead managers for Croatia's bond.
Indonesia's Telkom is unlikely to issue a bond in international capital markets this year, despite receiving proposals from foreign investment bankers, finance director Harry Supangkat said Monday.
"I don't think we should issue bonds this year as we still have the remaining IPO proceeds, but we certainly are considering the possibility," he said.

In developments from Asia's local currency bond markets, the Shanghai Securities News reported today that China's Finance Ministry plans to introduce a market maker system to the state debt secondary market in 1997.
